chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Salim al-Ji'abi informed me, saying: Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Hasani narrated to us, saying: Abu Musa Isa ibn Mihran al-Musta'tif narrated to us, saying: Affan ibn Muslim informed us, saying: Wuhayb narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Aisha who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family, saying:

"Indeed I shall be at the Pool, watching who among you comes to me, and surely some men will be pushed away from me. So I will say: O my Lord! My companions! My companions! Then it will be said: You do not know what they did after you. They continued to turn back on their heels, retreating backward."

key_terms.أصحابي: My companions - referring to the Sahaba, the companions of the Prophet
key_terms.الحوض: The Pool (Hawd) - a basin in the afterlife given to the Prophet (SAWW), often identified with al-Kawthar
key_terms.القهقري: Retreating backward, going in reverse - an idiom for apostasy and regression from faith

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about his companions at the Pool of Kawthar?
ai.summary: The Prophet (SAWW) foretold that on the Day of Judgment, he would be at the Pool of Kawthar and some of his companions would be driven away from him. When he intercedes for them, he is told they reneged after his death. This hadith, narrated through Aisha, was historically used by Shia scholars to demonstrate that not all companions remained faithful after the Prophet, and the expression "turning back on their heels" became a key phrase in debates about the post-prophetic succession crisis.
